January 15 35.

Dear Sarly,

I forward herewith for your information
tabulated statements relating to the arrest of
four communists named Tsang Kung Sing, Wong Ming Tuh,
Sung Dah Ming and Ting Bah during the night of
January 7/8, 1935 in the Hongkew district.

The accused appeared on remand before the
Second Branch Kiangsu High Court on January 12 when
they were ordered to be extradited to the Chinese
Authorities.

Photographs of the four accused are also
attached.

Yours sincerely,
JAG.

Monsieur R. Sarly,
Chief of the Political Section,
French Police.

during the night of January 7/8, 1935, in various parts of

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. 2, Special Branch Section
REPORT
Date January 11, 1935.
Subject Communist suspects arrested in the Hongkew District
on the night of January 7, 1935.
Made by D.S. Pitts. Forwarded by.

With reference to the attached file relating to the
arrests on the night of January 7, 1935 of
(1) Tsang Kung Sing (張更新) at 377 North Szechuen Road.
(2) Wong Ming Tuh (王明德) at 728 Zung Is Li (仁智里),
Woochung Road.
(3) Sung Dah Ming (申達明) at 120 Kyung Su Li (金書里),
Woosung Road and
(4) Ting Bah (丁白) at 16 Doong Sung Li (同生里),
Point Road,
apprehended in conjunction with the Bureau of Public Safety
at whose request the warrants were issued, I have to report that
the four accused have been very thoroughly interrogated regarding
their alleged communist activities and the reason as to why
they were in possession of "Red" literature, but they steadfastly
refuse to reveal any further information of importance other
than that contained in their original statements.
Sung Dah Ming (3) worked as a proof-reader at a
monthly salary of $16.00 from June 1933 until July 1934 at the
Chi Tse Book Company (啟智書局), Lane 116, No. 1 Rue des
Peres, off Rue du Consulat and resigned of his own free-will
in order to better himself. This has been confirmed by the
accountant of the concern in question which deals in perfectly
legitimate reading matter.
The accused, after resigning his position, stayed at
Fang Foo Fong (打浦坊), Route Pere Robert, until the end of
August with a friend named Yang Foo Long (楊福龍), whose
present whereabouts are unknown. In September, 1934, Sung
Dah Ming proceeded to Nanking in order to visit relatives, and
returned to Shanghai in the latter part of December, 1934, with

申达明（3）从1933年6月至1934年7月在启智书局（Chi Tse Book Company，位于领事馆路旁神父路116弄）担任校对员，月薪16.00元，后为求更好发展自愿辞职。此事已由该公司会计证实，该公司经营完全合法的读物。

My name is Chang Kung Hsin (          ), aged 33,
single, native of Laichow, Kwangtung Province, unemployed.
I am able to read and write, having studied in a
primary school in my native place.
For some eight years I acted as a teacher in a
primary school in Laichow and in 1933 I became acquainted
with one Jung Tse Yuan (          ), a teacher, who, as far
as I know, is still in Laichow.
He introduced me to several communist comrades in
1934 and I joined the party in February, 1934, in Laichow.
My duties in the Communist Party were to write pamphlets,
documents, messages, slogans, etc. for which I received
20.00 per month as salary.
I came to Shanghai about 4 months on the ss. "Sing-
kiang" in order to seek more congenial employment from a
former friend named Wang Tung Ming (          ).
I met Wang at the Ling Nan Hotel (          ),
Soochang Road, shortly after my arrival, but I do not know
his present whereabouts. He is a member of the Communist
Party and I received my instructions from him from time to time
during my first month in Shanghai when I was residing at
100 Tai An Li, North Szechwan Road.
I have not seen him since that period and I do not
know where he is living at present. He gave me the
duplicating material and communist literature found at my
residence by the police and I was merely minding it for him.
I am not an active communist and knew no other

本人名叫张公信（Chang Kung Hsin）（          ），33岁，未婚，广东省莱州人，无业。

My name is Ding Bai ( 丁白 ) age 23, a native
of Wusih, living at House No.16 Dong An Li, off Point
Road. I was a teacher for one year at a primary school
in Wusih. I came to Shanghai in August of last year
for the purpose of seeking a job. I have no friend in
Shanghai except my teacher named ___ ( 史 ), who is
teaching at the Zao Chen Little School in Nantao. I
have a mother but no father. I am now unemployed. The
Communist literature seized at my room belonged to one
named Chen Ming Ying ( 陈明英 ), whose address I do not
know. The age of Chen Ming Ying is 20 and he is as tall
as I. I have rented the room mentioned for about half
a month. Before renting the room, I worked without pay
for a monthly newspaper called "The New Children Newspaper"
on Beapoo Road near North Fukien Road. The man who
deposited the Communist literature in my room is a native
of Fukien, while the one who introduced me to the newspaper
office is a native of Wusih, aged 30. I visited the latter
one the other day, but he had left the newspaper already.
I am not a Communist.

(Signed)
